# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (seed child) — teach the prompt HOW grading works: hidden re-run + type-exact value compare
- Changes I made (all additive to prompt.md; original 6 rules kept verbatim):
  1. Added "How your code is graded" section: the final code is RE-RUN on 2 hidden input files with the SAME layout but DIFFERENT data → forbid hardcoding output / pasting sample or instruction-example values; require data-driven logic over the real extent (`ws.max_row`). (Cluster: overfit/hardcode — 5192, 3911, 38332.)
  2. Added the value-TYPE contract: grader compares by exact Python type on `.value` (numbers→round 2dp, datetimes→day serial, numeric-strings coerced but date-strings not) → write dates as real datetime, numbers as numbers, anchor to sample/adjacent type. (Cluster: type mismatch — 50630, 30709.)
  3. Added the "only cell VALUES are graded" fact: fill/font colors, number formats, formula text are NOT compared; put the answer in values; a formula counts only by its recalculated value. (Cluster: non-graded formatting — CF_11072.)
  4. Added a 5-item pre-save checklist making generalize + correct-type + range-only + exact-output_path preconditions of finishing. (Behavioral: writes final code without inspecting/verifying.)
- Expected effect + why safe: fixes the overfit/hardcode class (biggest cluster) and the date/number-type class; all four are ADDITIVE and match what the 24 passing tasks already do (general data-driven code, matching types; verified all 24 reference the literal `1_<id>_input` path). Blast radius BOUNDED. I deliberately did NOT strengthen "prefer literal values" into a formula ban because passing tasks 52021/46897/55060/55667/58109 write formulas and pass via LibreOffice recalc — a ban would regress them.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — this is the seed; LEDGER/JOURNAL/RUNMAP empty.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet. (Recorded for future: a global "always write literals, never formulas" edit is expected UNSAFE — 5 passing tasks depend on formula+recalc.)
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: complex Sheet-Level algorithm-correctness (110-2, 325-44, 450-9 — wrong transformation logic, not a shared prose gap; risk of overfitting if patched per-task) and robust date-format parsing (30709 cases 2/3). Infra: 73-45 (formula recalc failed — environment, handed back, do not optimize).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, measure which of clusters 1–3 moved; then consider a worked openpyxl example (last-row detection + writing a real datetime) if the type/generalization message under-delivers for the weaker reader; investigate the Sheet-Level algorithm failures individually only via general patterns (e.g. don't-truncate-to-preview-size), never task literals.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.620 Δ=+0.107 · fixed={47741, 50051, 51958, 73-45, CF_11072} · broke={353-29, 587-38}.

## Iteration cand_0002 — teach the agent that the previewed Output/example IS the spec: derive + self-verify against it
- Changes I made (all additive to prompt.md; cand_0001's sections kept verbatim):
  1. New section "The shown result is your specification — reproduce it, do not paste it":
     the `spreadsheet_content` preview frequently contains the demonstrated answer (a second
     "Output"/"wanted results" sheet, a pre-filled sample answer cell, an example column, or
     a worked "input→output" example in the instruction). Treat it as the exact transformation
     spec — derive the rule, row-expansion, column order and value types from it — and
     reproduce it by COMPUTING (never pasting). Includes a generic derive-vs-paste worked
     example. (Cluster: wrong transformation logic despite a demonstrated answer — 325-44,
     450-9, 110-2, 587-38, 5192, 353-29, 59259, +partial-credit 39046/51359/11842/30709/3911.)
  2. Checklist item 5 (new pre-save precondition): code must reproduce EVERY shown example on
     the visible data or the rule is wrong — "do not save a mismatch". Makes the self-test
     unavoidable, not advisory. (old item 5 "saved to output_path" → item 6.)
  3. New "implement exactly the stated conditional logic" line: blank→blank means write blank;
     no guessed/interpolated fallback the instruction didn't request; use the demonstration
     only for unspecified details, never to override an explicit rule. (Cluster: over-
     engineering — 59667 invented year-interpolation where instruction said return blank.)
- Per change, expected effect + why safe: edits 1+2 point the agent at the demonstrated
  answer it was already given and force a self-check against it (5192's code made `1456CH02A`
  vs stated `1456CH02`; 325-44 overwrote the previewed Output demo). BOUNDED/additive: the 27
  passers already reproduce their shown example column (verified 1563/46897/48354/41297), so
  the rule reinforces existing behavior; fires only when a demonstration is shown = the
  failing class. Edit 3 is additive; no passing task's gold answer relies on inventing
  unrequested fallback. No global decision/permission rule loosened; no formula ban added.
- Building on prior RESULTS: built on cand_0001 (ACCEPTED +0.107) — kept its hidden-re-run /
  type-exact-value-only / only-values-graded / no-hardcode content; ADD the missing
  derive-and-verify-against-the-shown-demonstration piece. cand_0001 broke {353-29, 587-38};
  I did NOT alter cand_0001's edits — I add the demonstration-matching lever that directly
  targets those two (both have a demonstrated expected result in the preview).
- Refuted hypotheses (do not re-test): global "always write literals / never formulas" ban is
  UNSAFE (cand_0001 note — 5 passing tasks pass via LibreOffice formula recalc).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: idiosyncratic per-task algorithms with no demonstrated
  answer (53367 boolean "out of order", 56996 dropdown price lookup, 55931 chart-position diff,
  38332 unique-count, 50630 sentence split) — no shared prose fix; would need per-task logic
  (overfit). Left to the cluster-1 self-test where an example exists.
- Plateau signal: n/a (2nd iteration, parent was +0.107). If this is rejected or flat, next
  lever to try: a compact `<example>` block with 1–2 full worked openpyxl solutions (read demo
  sheet → derive rule → compute → self-check) for the weaker reader, rather than more prose.
- Focus next iteration: measure whether the demonstration-matching lever moved the sheet-level
  cluster (325-44/450-9/110-2/587-38) and 5192; if it under-delivers for gpt-5.5, escalate to a
  worked full-code exemplar; otherwise attack the no-demonstration idiosyncratic tasks only via
  general sub-patterns (never task literals).

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.567 Δ=-0.053 · fixed={587-38} · broke={44266, 50051, 55667}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
